recommendation: #304 planner review: recommendations to the maintainer from fork I's analysis (14z-207)

For #304 (issue304.md) I recommend to the maintainer, on fork I's read-only analysis (REPORT.md) built on lane F's unlanded #313 fix: (1) option (b), one tracked list that classes each build/ top-level directory as a gate input or as scratch, held by a census gate that fails on an unclassed directory, rather than a per-gate allow-list, because the PILOT trace's untracked reads (ur.txt) include named build directories (m3b_merged31, pyron46, the emu_* records) that the registry does not declare and tools/tests name 105 build-dir families (build_names_in_code.txt); (2) the snapshot leaves out the scratch directories (build/agent*, build/sheets, build/rulecheck) and keeps build/static_runs and the other build/ inputs that 44 gates read (build_needs.txt), because scratch is 5,182,386 of the 5,241,597 listed files (snapshot_listing_prefixes.txt) and the copy step S2 measured at 166-207 us/file (snapsteps.txt) is what makes the median 971 s setup (snapshot_setup_records.txt), landing only after a Mac tier with scratch and one without are compared, since which gates fail or SKIP without scratch was not measured; (3) planner changes: prune scratch from the untracked listing (19,642 paths in 0.3-0.4 s against 26.5-26.9 s, snapsteps.txt, prof/f_head_1.log) with the 29 whole-tree R4 readers that cover scratch (r4_readers.txt) either always re-run or decided by a scratch-changed check, judge tracked changes first (predict 649.4 s to 118.5 s on the old base, prof/old_base_f_noscr_1.log, prof/old_base_f_noscr_tf_1.log), run the gate loop in 4 processes (106.9/95.7 s to 33.1/28.4 s, identical verdict files, prof/par_plan.log), and refuse with the prefixes named above about 5,000 effective untracked paths or past a time limit; (4) sharding across machines only if the tier is still too slow, since it needs a shard option, a merge writing one tier-all row and a maintainer change to the edit-locked green guard. Not tested: tiers with and without scratch in the snapshot; a read trace on the Mac, where the scratch lives (the trace is PILOT's, from lane F); the emulator tier's build/ needs; the parallel planner on PILOT or ERIS; the Mac timings ran beside the #291 sheet run (load 8 to 59), each taken twice; the 5,000-path threshold is a proposal from measured normals of 53 and 405 effective paths (prof/f_head_1.log, prof/old_base_f_head_1.log), not a measured cutoff.
